cards.title: One engine call core: a deadline and a typed error for every provider
acceptance: case 13: for each of text, vision, embed, speak, listen, a stub provider whose run never settles, called with timeoutMs 25 -> the engine function rejects within 1000 ms with an EngineError of kind 'timeout' and provider 'stub' (5 of 5 kinds; the test races a 1 s sentinel so a hang fails the case instead of stalling the suite) (tools/engines-rules-test.cjs)
case 14: the stub's run receives a second argument { signal }; after the timeout signal.aborted is true, after a fast success it is false (tools/engines-rules-test.cjs)

case 15: for each of the five kinds a stub that throws new Error('spawn piper ENOENT\n  at x') -> an EngineError of kind 'exit', provider 'stub', message the first line only; a stub that throws EngineError('unreachable','stub','x') -> that same object, kind still 'unreachable' (tools/engines-rules-test.cjs)

case 16: deadlineFor('text', provider without deadlineMs, {}) -> DEADLINE_MS.text; deadlineFor('text', provider with deadlineMs 240000, {timeoutMs: 90000}) -> 240000; deadlineFor('vision', p, {timeoutMs: 5000}) -> 5000; DEADLINE_MS has a finite positive number for all five kinds (tools/engines-rules-test.cjs)

case 17: a shorten re-ask whose second provider call never settles (timeoutMs 30) -> text() rejects with the FIRST shape EngineError (path 'topics[0].why'), after exactly 2 provider calls (tools/engines-rules-test.cjs)

GUARD case 18: codexCli.deadlineMs is 240000 and claudeCli.deadlineMs is undefined, so codex.ts:53's floor (Math.max(timeoutMs, 240000)) survives the move; a stub that answers at once resolves with its provider name and a numeric ms, for all five kinds; cases 1-12 stay green unchanged (tools/engines-rules-test.cjs)
premise: desk/src/lib/engines/types.ts:12-16 - TextRequest declares timeoutMs; VisionRequest, SpeakRequest, EmbedRequest and ListenRequest declare none (1 of 5 request types can be given a deadline)

desk/src/lib/engines/text.ts:59, codex.ts:53, listen.ts:43 - three deadline styles: a setTimeout that kills the child (claude, default 90000), a setTimeout with a 240000 floor (codex), AbortSignal.timeout(120000) (listen)

desk/src/lib/engines/vision.ts:28-31, embed.ts:18, voice.ts:46, voice.ts:67 - four provider paths with no deadline at all: two Ollama fetches and the ElevenLabs fetch pass no signal, the Piper spawn has no timer (4 of 7 provider run() paths; the fetch ones rest on the runtime's own default, the Piper one on nothing)

desk/src/lib/engines/types.ts:6-7 - the contract says every answer 'either resolves with that shape or rejects with an EngineError'; 7 lines throw something else: voice.ts:49 (p.on('error', reject) hands up the raw spawn Error), voice.ts:50 (new Error('piper exited ...')), voice.ts:53 (readFileSync), vision.ts:33 (res.json()), embed.ts:21 (res.json()), listen.ts:46 (r.json()), codex.ts:62 (readFile of last.txt); plus the temp-dir creations at voice.ts:42 and codex.ts:41

desk/src/lib/engines/shape.ts:96-102, embed.ts:30-35, listen.ts:55-57, voice.ts:81-83 - the same envelope written four times: started = Date.now(), provider(kind), await run(req), name = a.provider ?? p.name, ms (text and vision share the one in answer(); embed, listen and speak each hand-roll a copy)

desk/src/lib/desk/job.ts:76 - runJob refuses a second run of a kind while its job is 'running' (409 BUSY); desk/src/app/api/hint/route.ts:28 and desk/src/tv/keys.ts:195 refuse the same way; desk/src/app/api/session/retry/route.ts:28 only retries a 'failed' job; desk/src/lib/session/store.ts:202 settles a running job only when a SAVED session is loaded, i.e. on restart. So an engine call that never returns leaves its job 'running' and its screen waiting (desk/src/essay/EssayTV.tsx:139 captions 'Reading' while running) until the desk is reset or restarted
desk/src/lib/desk/job.ts:66 - jobError words the failure by EngineError.kind and falls back to a bare 'Try again.' for anything else, so the 7 raw throws above lose the desk's reason

tools/*.cjs - 22 files stub providers with run(req) (grep -l useProvider tools = 22); tools/lab-bench.cjs:121 and tools/calc-model-yield.cjs:137 wrap run(req) and drop any second argument, so the new argument must be optional and the core must enforce the deadline itself, not rely on a provider honouring the signal
cards.rollback: Three commits: test(engines) adds cases 13-18 red, refactor(engines) adds call.ts and moves answer(), embed(), listen(), speak() onto it, feat(engines) gives the Ollama, ElevenLabs, Piper and listen providers their abort handling and adds timeoutMs to the four request types. Every new parameter is optional and the old provider shape still type-checks, so reverting the last two commits restores today's behaviour and leaves the tests.
cards.runner_up: Cache synthesised speech by (provider, voice, text) so a repeated line (Linga's Hear it again, fixed first questions, 'Time for a break.') is not paid for twice: a new capability, gate direction, and it does not close a hang.
cards.body:
## Summary
Every engine call goes through one core that owns the deadline, the abort signal, the typed error and the provider/ms envelope. Today only text has a deadline you can set, five of the seven providers fail in ways the contract says they cannot, and the envelope is written four times.

## Description
The registry (registry.ts) and the shape rule (shape.ts) already made the engines one seam for WHICH provider runs and WHAT an answer must look like. They stopped short of HOW a call ends. A call ends one of three ways, and the engines implement each differently per provider:

- Deadline: claude kills its child on a timer (text.ts:59), codex does the same with a 240 s floor that overrides the caller (codex.ts:53), listen aborts a fetch (listen.ts:43), and four paths have none (vision.ts:28-31, embed.ts:18, voice.ts:46 Piper, voice.ts:67 ElevenLabs). Only TextRequest can carry timeoutMs (types.ts:12), so even a caller that wanted a vision or speech deadline could not say so.
- Failure: types.ts:6-7 promises a typed EngineError, but seven lines throw a plain Error or SyntaxError (voice.ts:49, 50, 53; vision.ts:33; embed.ts:21; listen.ts:46; codex.ts:62). job.ts:66 words a failure from EngineError.kind and drops to 'Try again.' for these, so the operator and the learner lose the reason.
- Success: the started/provider/run/name/ms envelope is written in answer() (shape.ts:96-102) and again, by hand, in embed(), listen() and speak().

Why this is the structural move and not tidying: a hung engine call is not a slow request, it is a stuck desk. runJob refuses a second run while the job is running (job.ts:76), the hint route and the TV key rule refuse the same way (hint/route.ts:28, keys.ts:195), retry only accepts a failed job (retry/route.ts:28), and a running job is settled only on restart (store.ts:202). So one vision stall in `read` leaves the page 'Reading' with no retry. The deadline belongs to the engine seam, once.

The move: a new call.ts exports `DEADLINE_MS` (per kind: text 90000, vision 180000, embed 60000, speak 30000, listen 120000), `deadlineFor(kind, provider, req)` (req.timeoutMs, else the kind's default, floored by an optional `Provider.deadlineMs` so codex keeps its 240000) and `call(kind, provider, req)`, which runs the provider with an AbortSignal, races it against the deadline, passes an EngineError through untouched, turns anything else into an EngineError of kind 'exit' with the first line of its message, and returns `{answer, provider, ms}`. answer() (text, vision, codexText), embed(), listen() and speak() each become a call to it. Providers drop their private timers and honour `ctx.signal`: the claude and codex children are killed on abort, the Ollama and ElevenLabs fetches get the signal, Piper's child is killed. VisionRequest, EmbedRequest, SpeakRequest and ListenRequest gain an optional timeoutMs.

Contract note (gate `contract`): `Provider.run(req, ctx?)` gains an optional second parameter and `Provider.deadlineMs?` is new; both are optional, so the 22 test files that stub run(req) are unaffected. Consumers of the changed behaviour: lib/desk/read.ts and mark.ts (vision), lib/library/lessons.ts (embed), api/speak and api/listen (routes keep their fixed 502 bodies), api/smoke, lib/desk/job.ts (kind -> sentence), tools/lab-bench.cjs and tools/calc-model-yield.cjs (wrappers that drop the second argument; the core still enforces the deadline).

## Flow
- A route or pipeline calls text(), vision(), embed(), speak() or listen() exactly as today.
- The engine function hands its provider and request to call(); the deadline is the request's timeoutMs, else the kind's default, floored by the provider's own.
- The provider runs with a signal. On the deadline the core aborts the signal and rejects with EngineError('timeout', providerName, ...); on a plain throw it rejects with EngineError('exit', ...) carrying the first line only.
- answer() still parses and validates; a shorten re-ask is a second call() with its own deadline, and if it hangs the first shape rejection stands.
- runJob receives a typed error in every case, so the job ends 'failed' with the desk's reason and the existing Try again path works.

## Expected impact
The desk can no longer be left waiting on a hung engine: every call ends in a typed result within a stated time, and the one place that states the times is a table in call.ts instead of three styles and four gaps. Piper, which has no timer at all today, stops being able to hold /api/speak and a child process forever. A new provider (Bedrock, Polly, named in four file headers as 'later') gets deadline, abort and error mapping by implementing run(), not by remembering to.

## Evaluation
Claim: every engine kind ends a call within its deadline with a typed EngineError, and the call envelope exists once.
Before: 0 of 5 acceptance cases pass (case 13 hangs for 5 of 5 kinds, case 15 fails for 5 of 5, plus the 4-of-7 and 7-site counts above)
After: 5 of 5 pass, plus 1 declared guard
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first
Result: better
Gate: contract

cards.title: Engine check answers in seconds: what would run, whether it answers, what to fix
acceptance: case 19: stubs for all five kinds, each with a probe and a run that counts its calls -> engineStatus() returns 5 rows in the order text, vision, embed, speak, listen, each { kind, provider: 'stub', ok, say, ms }, and no run() was called (tools/engines-rules-test.cjs)

case 20: a stub probe that never answers, with budgetMs 30 -> that row is { ok: false, say: /did not answer/ } while the other four rows are unaffected, and the whole call returns in under 500 ms (probes run in parallel, not one after another) (tools/engines-rules-test.cjs)

desk/src/lib/engines/vision.ts:16 and embed.ts:12 - the two Ollama engines name their models (qwen3.8:27b, nomic-embed-text); a missing pull surfaces only as a later 404 inside a page read ('ollama 404: ...' truncated, vision.ts:32) rather than as a line the operator can act on

grep -rn 'smoke' tools uat desk/src -> only app/api/smoke/route.ts and app/page.tsx:16 (the 'Engine check' link): the one operator-facing health surface has 0 tests, and desk/README.md:30 describes it as 'one call per engine'
cards.rollback: Two commits after the red tests: feat(engines) adds optional Provider.probe, health.ts and the per-provider probes, then feat(smoke) swaps the route onto health.ts and updates the README line. Probes are optional and additive; reverting the second commit restores the old route unchanged, reverting both removes the probes and leaves the tests.
cards.runner_up: Read engine env once through one lazy config (text.ts:24-25, embed.ts:11-12, vision.ts:15-16 and voice.ts:27-32 read process.env at import; listen.ts:16-22 and codex.ts:20 read per call; the Ollama host line is written twice) so a test can flip Piper or the host and the check can print the effective config.
cards.body:
## Summary
The Engine check link on the desk landing page (app/page.tsx:16) becomes a status the operator can read at a glance. It lists all five engines with the provider that would run, whether it answers and what to do when it does not, in about two seconds and with no model call. A `?live=1` run does the real calls in parallel.

## Description
The route's own comment says its job: 'a broken engine is found here and not on the TV' (smoke/route.ts:1). It does that job slowly and partially. It runs the text, embed and vision calls in series (route.ts:14-20), so the answer arrives after the sum of the slowest three. It covers 3 of the 5 engines, mislabels a Piper-only desk as 'key present' (route.ts:12), omits listen although listenStatus() exists (listen.ts:27), never says which provider is active although activeProvider() was written for exactly that (registry.ts:36) and nothing in desk/src calls it, and on failure prints the engine's own message (route.ts:13), the class of leak 4772d195 closed on the speech routes. A paired phone, not only the TV, can start the three model calls, because the route never reads the role.

The operator's real questions are cheap to answer from facts the desk already holds: which provider would run, is its binary or host reachable, is the model pulled, is the key or the voice file there. Those need a probe, not a model call.

The move: an optional `Provider.probe(): Promise<{ ok: boolean; say: string }>` (types.ts) implemented by each provider in one or two lines of real checking: claude-cli resolves its binary, codex resolves its launcher (codex.ts launcher()), the two Ollama engines GET /api/tags and look for their model (so a missing model says 'ollama pull qwen3.8:27b' and an unreachable host says 'ollama serve' with the host), Piper checks its two paths, ElevenLabs checks the key is set without calling it, listen reuses listenStatus(). A new `health.ts` exports `engineStatus(budgetMs)`, which asks each kind's ACTIVE provider (activeProvider) for its probe in parallel under a budget and returns rows `{ kind, provider, ok: boolean | null, say, ms }` (null when a provider has no probe, never a guess), and `engineCheck({ live, sample })`, which for `live` also runs text, vision (when a sample page exists), embed and speak in parallel and reports the engine's own provider and ms, with failures as `{ kind, say }` from the EngineError kind and the detail sent to console.error as job.ts does. The route returns those rows, runs live only on `?live=1`, and answers a phone 403 (the TV, or an in-process caller with no role header, may ask).

Contract note (gate `contract`): the route's response shape changes. Its consumers: app/page.tsx:16 (a plain link, no parse), desk/README.md:30 (prose, updated here), no script or test reads it today (grep above). The 403 for a paired phone tightens who may start model calls; it does not open any route to a guest, so the pairing rule in proxy.ts is untouched.

## Flow
- The operator opens Engine check from the TV's browser: five rows appear at once, e.g. text claude-cli ok, vision ollama NOT ok 'ollama pull qwen3.8:27b', embed ollama ok, speak piper ok, listen gravitone ok.
- A row that is not ok says what to do in one line.
- To prove a path end to end, the operator adds ?live=1: the real calls run side by side and each row reports its provider and milliseconds.
- A paired phone that loads the same address gets 403 and no engine is touched.

## Expected impact
The first thing an operator does when a page read or a hint fails is open this check; today that is a wait of up to a couple of minutes for a JSON dump that skips listen, mislabels Piper and names no provider. After the change the same question takes two seconds, covers all five engines, and the commonest failures (Ollama down, model not pulled, no CLI, no key, STT not running) each read as an instruction. A child's phone can no longer spend model calls by loading a URL.

## Evaluation
Claim: the engine check reports all five engines with their active provider and a fix line in one parallel round, without a model call, and a phone cannot start the live run.
Before: 0 of 6 acceptance cases pass (the route runs 3 live calls in series, covers 3 of 5 engines, has no probe, no role check and no test)
After: 6 of 6
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first
Result: better
Gate: contract
